chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When you intend to wash the deceased, place a cloth between you and him to cover his private part from you, whether it is a shirt or something else. Then begin with his hands and his head, washing them three times with lotus leaves, then the rest of his body, and begin with his right side.

When you intend to wash his private part, take a clean rag and wrap it around your left hand, then insert your hand from beneath the cloth that is on the deceased's private part, and wash it without seeing his nakedness.

When you finish washing him with lotus leaves, wash him again with water and camphor, and something of his perfume. Then wash him with pure water with another washing, until when you have finished the three (washings), place him in a cloth, then dry him.
ai.seo_question: What is the step-by-step procedure for washing a deceased person in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* establishes the foundational methodology for *ghusl al-mayyit*, emphasizing the preservation of modesty (*awrah*) through the 'no direct sight' technique during the washing of the private parts. It prescribes a structured purification sequence using sidr (lotus leaves), camphor, and musk, reflecting the Shia emphasis on both physical cleanliness and spiritual dignity in preparing the deceased for burial.
